finding: §3.4/§11.4 require --status to recompute each round's cleanliness from its surviving findings' severities under the current review_converge_on, but §4.3 only guarantees a `by_severity` breakdown computed at merge time over ALL merged findings. Surviving != merged: a finding resolved wontfix/duplicate (§3.5) must be excluded, and resolutions can change AFTER a round is recorded. The spec never states what exactly is persisted on the round (a merge-time by_severity snapshot? per-finding {severity, resolution}? nothing but a stored clean flag plus a live re-read of the findings file?) nor how --status combines the stored severity data with the CURRENT resolution state. Building this correctly needs that persisted structure and the overlay rule defined: if it stores merge-time by_severity, a round whose mediums were all resolved would wrongly recompute as not-clean under `all`.
suggestion: State precisely what each recorded round persists for recompute (e.g. the severity of each surviving finding, or a count-by-severity of unresolved findings), and specify that --status recomputes surviving-set severities by overlaying the CURRENT resolution state from .tp-review over that record — so that both a converge_on change (§3.4) and a post-record wontfix (§3.5) are reflected. Clarify whether the persisted breakdown is over surviving (post-resolution) findings or all merged findings.

finding: §3.3 defines review_converge_on with exactly two legal values (`blocking`, `all`) and §10.1 confirms no third value is allowed, but the spec never states the error path for an invalid value: what `tp set --workflow review_converge_on=foo` (and an invalid value coming from env or .tp/config.json) does — the exit code (1/2/3/4) and the hint the agent receives. Other workflow fields have enumerated/ranged validation; this one leaves rejection behavior for the implementer to invent.
suggestion: Specify that an unrecognized review_converge_on value is rejected with a stated exit code and an actionable hint (e.g. `must be one of: blocking, all`), consistent with how other workflow-field validation errors are reported, and state the behavior for an invalid value arriving via env/project config vs a resolved fallback.

finding: §4.2 and Test 7 require --status and --record to 'report the count of surviving non-blocking findings and that they were accepted open', but no JSON field name is given for either the count or the 'accepted open' signal. A deterministic pass/fail test needs the observable field names; two engineers would assert on differently-named fields.
suggestion: Pin the field name(s) in the --status/--record output that carry the surviving-non-blocking count and the accepted-open indicator.

finding: §7.2 requires --verify and code-audit findings to also carry a `role` field, and Test 12 asserts they 'also carry role', but the exact role value is pinned only for regression (role: "regression"). The value verify and code-audit findings must carry is left to interpretation, so two engineers write different assertions (e.g. "verifier" vs "verify", "code-audit" vs "auditor").
suggestion: State the exact role string each emitting perspective stamps (regression, verify, code-audit) so the assertion is deterministic.

finding: The release adds several new emitted JSON keys to review/audit --status and --record output — next_action (§8.1), harness_note and harness_stale (§6.3), and the surviving-non-blocking-findings count (§4.2) — but the spec never mentions --compact, tp's defining token-reduction lever (P3, Minimal Tokens). CLAUDE.md's convention explicitly enumerates the fields --compact omits; adding output keys without declaring their compact behavior leaves each new byte in every response an agent parses on the always-on path, which is exactly the AX cost this tool exists to minimize. next_action in particular is advisory/read-only and a natural strip candidate.
suggestion: State each new output field's --compact behavior in §4.2/§6.3/§8.1 (and add an acceptance item under §11): specify that next_action is stripped under --compact (advisory, derivable), and decide/declare whether harness_note/harness_stale and the surviving-non-blocking count survive compaction or are omitted, matching the existing 'compact omits X' contract.

finding: next_action is defined to name exactly one command, but §8.2 lists three triggering conditions (unresolved findings present; a mechanize_candidates class present; converged) without a precedence order for when more than one holds simultaneously. A recorded state can have BOTH unresolved findings AND a mechanize candidate; two engineers would write contradictory assertions about which command next_action returns. Test 14 asserts 'one command matched to state' but cannot be made deterministic without a stated tie-break order.
suggestion: State an explicit precedence (e.g. unresolved findings > mechanize candidate > forward command) and add an acceptance case fixing next_action's value when multiple triggers co-occur.

finding: next_action keys one of its branches on 'a mechanize_candidates class present -> register a check', and test #14 repeats 'register a check when a mechanize candidate exists', but no section of the spec defines mechanize_candidates: what produces it, when it is 'present', or where a reader sees it. The other next_action triggers (unresolved findings, converged) map to concepts the spec defines; this one dangles on an undefined term, so the condition cannot be evaluated or tested against the spec text.
suggestion: Define the mechanize_candidates concept in §8 (or cite the existing tp feature that surfaces it and the recorded field/class it reads), so the trigger condition and test #14 have a specified source.

finding: next_action's trigger list contradicts blocking-convergence. Under the new default review_converge_on: blocking, a round is clean and can converge while unresolved non-blocking (medium/low) findings still survive on the record — §4.2 explicitly accepts them open with no resolution required. But §8.2 (and test #14) enumerate the triggers as 'unresolved findings present -> resolve/verify; ... ; converged -> forward command' with no stated precedence. For the flagship state (converged under blocking with open medium findings) both conditions hold; read top-to-bottom the 'unresolved findings present' branch fires first, so next_action would say 'resolve them' and never emit the forward command, defeating §4.2's 'accepted open, no resolution required' design.
suggestion: Scope §8.2's 'unresolved findings present' trigger to unresolved BLOCKING findings (or state that convergence takes precedence over the resolve/verify trigger), so a round converged under `blocking` with only non-blocking findings open emits the forward command. Mirror the scoping in test #14.

finding: §8.1/§8.2 and Test 14 trigger a next_action of 'register a check' on 'a mechanize_candidates class present' / 'a mechanize candidate exists', but the spec never defines what constitutes a mechanize candidate — which finding class(es) or condition sets the flag, and what field carries it. A tester cannot construct the triggering state deterministically, so Test 14's 'register a check when a mechanize candidate exists' branch is non-verifiable.
suggestion: Define the mechanize_candidates trigger precisely (the exact finding class/condition and the state field that surfaces it), or reference the existing definition if it predates this spec.

finding: harness_stale conflates two distinct empty-note cases. --harness-note is opt-in (§6.2, §10.5), so a post-release round can carry an empty note simply because the operator did not pass the flag. §6.3 scopes the 'empty means compatible' exemption only to 'when a round predates the field', so a latest round with a note whose immediately-prior post-release round opted out (empty note, not a predate) falls under 'the two most recently recorded rounds carry different notes' -> harness_stale=true. That spuriously signals 'a wrapper that changed mid-loop' when the operator merely omitted the flag, contradicting the intent that an absent note record nothing (§6.2).
suggestion: State in §6.3 whether an opt-out (post-release absent) note is treated as compatible like a predate, or as a distinct value that can differ from a present note; the natural choice consistent with §6.2 is that only two DIFFERENT non-empty notes set harness_stale, with any empty (predate or opt-out) treated as no-signal.

finding: §6.3 defines harness_stale as 'true when the two most recently recorded rounds carry different notes' and false when they match or a round predates the field, but never states the value when fewer than two rounds are recorded (a single recorded round, or the very first record). The natural inference is false, but leaving it unstated forces the implementer to guess the boundary that tests will assert (§11.11 only exercises the two-round cases).
suggestion: State the harness_stale value explicitly for the fewer-than-two-recorded-rounds case (e.g. false when there is no prior round to compare against), matching the 'empty means compatible' rule referenced for roles_hash.

finding: §6.3 defines harness_stale as true when 'the two most recently recorded rounds carry different notes' and false when they match or a round predates the field — but leaves the fewer-than-two-rounds case undefined (a single recorded round with a note has no prior round to compare). Test 11 cannot deterministically assert harness_stale for the first recorded round. The field name carrying the note text in --status output (Test 10/11) is also unpinned.
suggestion: Specify harness_stale for the single-round (and zero-round) case (presumably false), and name the --status field that reports the latest harness note.

finding: §8.2 keys a next_action branch on 'a mechanize_candidates class present', but mechanize_candidates is never defined anywhere in this spec (only over-specification is introduced, in §5). The implementer building the register-a-check branch cannot know what field/class presence triggers it or how it is detected without a definition or a cross-reference to the existing feature it names.
suggestion: Define mechanize_candidates in this spec or cite the existing feature/section that defines it (the class/output field name and what marks a finding as a mechanize candidate), so the next_action branch condition is buildable without guessing.
